Mañjuśrī has made various offerings to the Buddhas of the past; with sovereign wisdom, he is skillfully able to penetrate all dharmas, speaking in accordance with the Dharma and speaking according to reality, and he pays reverent homage to the Tathāgata.
He seized a sharp sword and rushed swiftly toward the Buddha.
The Buddha said, "Stop, stop, Mañjuśrī!
I have already been slain; I have been thoroughly slain."

"If there were even a slight convergence or aggregation of dharmas that could definitively be named Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, mother, father, or Arhat, and if there were anything to be grasped through transgression, then one could not be liberated."
One should know that those phenomena have no substance and do not exist; they are neither suchness nor reality; they are unproduced and unarisen, empty like illusions and transformations.
Therefore, regarding these phenomena, there is no person who incurs transgression, nor is there any transgression to be found.

"In this way, in this way," they reflected and understood well; having thus understood, those five bodhisattvas immediately attained the patience toward the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Having attained this patience, they were filled with joy and leaped up into the air—not far from the ground, at the height of seven *tāla* trees—and spoke these verses:
"All phenomena are like illusions, All arise from conceptual construction."
This does not exist determinately; all phenomena are empty.
The mind falsely discriminates, and through delusion, one grasps at the notion of a self.
Recalling past lives, one wonders: "What evil deeds did I commit?"
In the past, I committed the most grievous evil deeds: killing my parents, who are a field of supreme merit; killing an Arhat; and killing a Bhikṣu.
As the retribution for those evil karmas, I ought to undergo suffering and affliction.
Now, in the presence of virtuous persons, one hears the Dharma and eliminates doubt and regret.
If the mind does not abandon remorse and regret, yet remembers those of great renown,
understands and awakens to the dharma-realm— where would there be no afflictions?
The Buddha’s skillful means—knowing the Sage through his means—by what power of means does he purify the doubts and regrets of sentient beings?
All phenomena are empty and without essence; they are neither Buddha, nor Dharma, nor Saṅgha.
Parents cannot be found; there is no such thing as an Arhat, nor is there even a slight dharma that kills, nor is there even a slight dharma that falls.
All dharmas have the characteristic of equality, abiding in that very same equality.
Mañjuśrī of great wisdom, having already realized such a Dharma,
took up a sharp sword in his hand and ran swiftly toward the Tathāgata.
As the sharp sword and as the Buddha, those two were without any difference in appearance.
"Neither born nor real—within this, there is no person who kills.

When this Dharma-gate of grasping the iron sword was spoken, the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, shook in six ways; the great earth trembled violently, and all worlds rose up.

At that time, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions—each currently existing, living, and abiding—had attendants who each questioned their respective Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"By whose power has this great earth been shaken, such that the entire world has arisen?
That Buddha replied,
"O son of good family!"
There is a buddha-world named Sahā; therein dwells a buddha titled Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is preaching the Dharma for the sake of the assembly.

In that Sahā world, there is a youth bodhisattva mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī, who has attained non-retrogression on the path to enlightenment. Grasping a sharp iron sword—a sword of wisdom—he hastens toward the Buddha in order to instruct and awaken the other bodhisattvas.
"Because he possesses sovereign power and knows his own capability, by these causes and conditions he causes the great earth to tremble.

At that time, the World-Honored One, relying on the sword of wisdom and speaking according to the true nature of reality (tathatā), caused the eyes of incalculable sentient beings to become pure, their minds to attain liberation, the faculty of patience (kṣānti) to arise, and their desire to practice for bodhi.

At that time, by the power of his sustaining presence, the World-Honored One sustained and protected those beings within this assembly who had initially given rise to only slight roots of goodness, as well as those with false discrimination and various conceptualizations, so that those beings would not see iron swords and would neither hear nor listen to this Dharma-gate of grasping the sword that was being taught.
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra said to the youth Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī!
You have committed an extremely evil karma of saṃsāra, desiring to kill a physician.”
"If this karma ripens, in what place will it be experienced?
Mañjuśrī said, "Venerable Śāriputra!"
"All have performed evil karma, yet since my birth I have never done such a thing; I do not know where this action will ripen.
Venerable Śāriputra!
Where does the illusory person’s illusory karma ripen? It ripens for me in this very way."
Why is this? Because an illusory person does not give rise to discrimination and is without falsehood.
Venerable Śāriputra!
All phenomena are like illusions and transformations.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, I now ask you; answer as you see fit.
"What do you think?
Can you obtain an iron sword?
He replied:
"There is none. [The Buddha asked:
"Can you perceive any evil karma that you possess?
He replied:
"No. "Have you attained the fruit? He replied:
“There is not. “Venerable Śāriputra!
If there were no iron, no karma, and no retribution, where would karma ripen?”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra said: "Mañjuśrī,
for what reason do you speak thus?"
Mañjuśrī said: "There is not even the slightest ripening of karmic retribution. Why is this?"
"Because all dharmas are without karma, without retribution, and without the ripening of karmic retribution.
At that time, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had come from the worlds of the ten directions addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

I only pray that the World-Honored One will empower the youth Mañjuśrī with his majestic spiritual power, enabling him to travel to the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions and preach the Dharma in this manner, just as I have come to this Buddha-world.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī said to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:
"O sons of good family, each of you should observe your own buddha-field."

At that time, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each observed their own buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions; each heard the voice of the youth Mañjuśrī within their own buddha-world, and each saw the youth Mañjuśrī standing before his Buddha, preaching this Dharma-gate to the great assembly. In each case, the Devaputra Susthitamati questioned this Dharma-gate, and in each case there were assemblies of bodhisattvas and devaputras present.
Having seen this, they attained what they had never experienced before and all exclaimed in praise: "Rare, rare!
Now this youth Mañjuśrī, while remaining unmoved within this Buddha-world, manifests universally in all places and is seen by all."
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī spoke these words to those bodhisattvas:
"Good sons! It is like a master illusionist who, having well studied the arts of illusion, displays various forms while remaining unmoved from his seat."

In this way, a bodhisattva who has skillfully studied the illusion of the *prajñāpāramitā* can, within the nature of illusory phenomena, universally manifest all Buddha-worlds according to whatever they recollect in their mind.
"Why is this? Because all dharmas are like illusions; thus should it be known.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke to the youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
“Mañjuśrī! Just as when the Tathāgatas appear in the world, so it is with hearing this Dharma-gate;
just as when a person realizes the fruit of a srotāpanna, so it is with hearing this Dharma-gate.”
Just as it is for one who has realized the fruit of a sakṛdāgāmin, so it is for one who hears this Dharma-gate;
just as it is for one who has realized the fruit of an anāgāmin, so it is for one who hears this Dharma-gate;
just as it is for one who has realized the dharma of an arhat, so it is for one who hears this Dharma-gate.
"Hearing this Dharma-gate and giving rise to faith and understanding is like sitting upon the seat of enlightenment; hearing this Dharma-gate is likewise so.
The youth Mañjuśrī said to the Buddha, "So it is, World-Honored One!"

It is like the equality of space; it is like the equality of signlessness; it is like the equality of wishlessness; it is like the equality of suchness; it is like the equality of the dharma-realm; it is like the equality of the limit of reality; it is like the equality of equality; it is like the equality of liberation; it is like the equality of detachment.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We only pray that the World-Honored One will protect this Dharma-gate so that, in future ages and at the end of the era, during the final fifty years, it may be widely circulated and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa, enabling all sons and daughters of good family to hear it.”
At that time, the celestial beings and humans throughout the trichiliocosm sounded drums and music;
all the flowering trees blossomed profusely, producing various kinds of flowers.
This entire trichiliocosm trembled, emitting a great radiance that filled the world, eclipsing the light of the sun and moon so that they no longer appeared.

Sixty-four billion times one hundred thousand devas rejoiced and leaped for joy, giving rise to a sense of wonder. Abiding in the void, they rained down celestial flowers, incense, powdered incense, and unguents as thick as falling rain; they played celestial music and, with palms joined, cried out in unison:
"Well-spoken is this most supreme and wondrous Dharma, this marvelous and excellent Dharma!"

Now that we have heard this Dharma-gate spoken by the youth Mañjuśrī, it is as if we have been born again among human beings in this world and have once more witnessed the turning of the wheel of Dharma.

If there are sentient beings who, upon hearing this Dharma-gate, are able to believe and understand it without being startled or terrified, you should know that these persons have certainly not come from meager merit.
"If there are sentient beings who have already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past, they shall hear this profound Dharma-gate without being startled or terrified.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Now a sign has appeared: this Dharma-gate of the sutra shall be maintained without extinction and will be widely propagated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future age.
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī!"
"Now there is a sign appearing: this Dharma-gate of the sutra shall abide and not perish.
Mañjuśrī said, "So it is, World-Honored One!"
"Truly act as its preserver, so that this Dharma-gate may long abide in the world.
The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!"

If it is true and a word of truth that one attains the realization of nirvana through the three gates of liberation, then it is also true and a word of truth that this Dharma-gate of the sutra shall be widely circulated and propagated throughout Jambudvīpa in the future, in the final age, during the last fifty years.

Mañjuśrī said: "If what the World-Honored One has taught—that there is no self, no sentient being, no life-force, no person, no human, no manava, and neither defilement nor purity—is the true and real word, then it is the true and real word that this Dharma-gate of the sutra will be widely practiced and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa in the future, during the final age of the five hundred years."
"If the Blessed One says it is not greed, hatred, or delusion; not name, not form; not cause, not view;
not existence, not consciousness; not body, not bodily intimation; not mind, not mental intimation;
not recollection, not mindfulness; not place, not movement in a place; not..."
It is not form, not feeling, not perception, not formations, and not consciousness; it is not the eye, not forms;
not the ear, not sounds; not the nose, not odors; not the tongue, not tastes; not the body, not tangibles;
not the mind, not phenomena; it is not the desire realm, not the form realm, and not the formless realm.
The realm of form is neither annihilated nor eternal; this is the true word of truth.
This Dharma-gate from this sutra shall be widely circulated and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future degenerate age; this is the true word of truth.
“If the Blessed One speaks of that which is not a stream-enterer, nor the fruit of stream-entry;
not a once-returner, nor the fruit of once-returning; not a non-returner, nor the fruit of non-returning;
not an arhat, nor the qualities of an arhat; not a pratyekabuddha, nor the qualities of a pratyekabuddha;”
It is not the Tathāgata, nor the qualities of a Tathāgata; it is not the powers, nor the fearlessnesses; it is not perception, nor consciousness;
it is not emptiness, nor signlessness, nor wishlessness; it is not desirelessness, nor intrinsic nature;
it is not attainment, nor realization; it is not accumulation, nor clarity, nor liberation; it is not the further shore.
It is not the middle, nor this shore; it is not nirvana, nor a name, nor indeterminate—this is the true, true word.
That this Dharma-gate of the sutra shall be widely circulated and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future degenerate age—this is the true, true word.

“If the Blessed One has spoken this true and real word—that there is truly no person who associates or dissociates, nor who joins or disperses—and that this Dharma-gate of the sutra will be widely circulated and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future and the end times, then this is a true and real word.”
"So it is, World-Honored One!

If the former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have already declared that there is not even the slightest dharma by which a sentient being attains liberation—neither attaining nirvāṇa, nor the existence of a sentient being, nor the arising of a dharma, nor the cessation of a dharma, nor loss, nor movement—then as they spoke of the past, so too for the future and the present, all such declarations are words of true reality.
This Dharma-gate of the sutra will be widely circulated and propagated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the latter age; this is a word of true reality."

"So it is, World-Honored One! If one says that in this Dharma there is not even the slightest dharma spoken—that it is not speech, not an utterance, not the expression of words; that it is not an ultimate teaching, not a teaching for a later time, not a teaching for the present; that it is not a teaching of echoes, not a teaching repeated again and again, and not a teaching of this Dharma; and that not a single word is spoken as this Dharma—then it is a true and real word that no one hears it now, no one will hear it in the future, and no one attains liberation. It is a true and real word that this Dharma-gate of the sutra shall widely circulate and spread throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future and the末代 (final age)."

“If the Blessed One’s declaration that this precept is neither precept nor the fruit of precept, neither samādhi nor the basis of samādhi, neither prajñā nor the fundamental wisdom of prajñā, and neither liberation nor the knowledge of liberation is true and real speech, then it is true and real speech that this Dharma-gate of the sūtra will widely circulate and spread throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future degenerate age.”

“If the Blessed One says that within the Dharma of the bodhisattvas there is no giving or renunciation, no guarding of precepts, no cultivation of patience, no arousal of diligence, no certainty in dhyāna, and no practice of prajñā; if he says there is no seeking of bodhi, no turning of the true practice, no attainment of bodhi, no attainment of powers, no attainment of fearlessness, no faculties, no rightness, no turning of the wheel of Dharma, and no liberating of sentient beings through speech—yet this is the true and real word—if this Dharma-gate of the sutra is widely circulated and propagated throughout Jambudvīpa during the final fifty years of the future and the末代 (final age), then this is the true and real word.”
When this Dharma was being taught, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"For what cause and condition does this world shake so greatly?
The World-Honored One then addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, saying: "Maitreya!"
"Do not speak such words now; if sentient beings with little faith hear this, they will be unable to understand it and will give rise to fear.
Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“If the Tathāgata were to speak [of this], many would gain strength, and there would be much benefit, peace, and happiness for devas and humans.
The Buddha said, “Maitreya!”

In the past, seventy-four billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddhas have taught this Dharma-gate at this very place, while the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta and the Devaputra Susīma engaged in dialogue and debate on its meaning.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How long has it been since the youth Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and the Devaputra Susthitamati accompanied one another to hear this Dharma-gate? Under which Buddha did they hear this Dharma-gate?”
The Buddha said: "Maitreya!

In the distant past, at the limit of seven hundred thousand asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Samantakusuma-siṃhagati-jaya-guṇasaṃcaya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"In this way, son of good family, you heard this Dharma-gate from that Buddha.

When he spoke these words, sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; twice that number attained non-retrogressive patience (*avaivartika-kṣānti*); and twice that number attained the stainless Dharma-eye (*vimala-dharmacakṣus*).

When the World-Honored One had finished expounding this Dharma-gate, the bhikṣus, the youth Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, the Devaputra Susthitamati, along with the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly filled with joy.
